item.research_question: Can a high-entropy alloy with the composition Al0.5CrMoNbTa0.5 be successfully produced using Selective Electron Beam Melting (SEBM) from a blend of elemental powders, and what are the resulting microstructural and compositional characteristics?
item.material_system: Al0.5CrMoNbTa0.5 multi-principle alloy (elemental powder blend of Al, Cr, Mo, Nb, Ta)
item.processing_route: Selective Electron Beam Melting (SEBM) using an ARCAM EBM A2 machine; build temperature 920 °C, layer thickness 50 μm, beam speed 80 mm/s, beam current 20 mA (energy density 15 J/mm); two-stage preheat-melt process with semi-sintering; no process parameter optimization was performed.
item.test_conditions: Post-manufacturing heat treatment in vacuumed quartz ampules for 24 hours at 1000 °C and 1300 °C; microstructure examined via SEM/EPMA (20 kV) and XRD (20–80°); chemical composition analyzed via SEM/EPMA.
key_findings: The as-built sample contained 8.4 at % Al instead of the designed 12.0 at % due to evaporation during printing.
The as-manufactured microstructure consisted of two solid solutions: an Al-poor phase (TaMoNb-based, ~1.4 at % Al) and an Al-rich phase (~11.8 at % Al).
Heat treatment at 1000 °C reduced Al content to 8.0 at % and Cr to 24.7 at %.
Heat treatment at 1300 °C further reduced Al to 7.8 at % and Cr to 23.2 at %.
Significant residual porosity was observed in all samples, attributed to non-optimized process parameters.
Heat treatment improved microstructural homogenization but did not reduce residual porosity.
Splatter droplets ('fireworks') contained all five elements, indicating they did not significantly alter the bulk composition of solid samples.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the compositional changes to the evaporation of light metals (Al and Cr) due to high vapor pressure at the electron beam molten pool temperature (up to 2500 °C) and the vacuum environment (10−3 mbar). The formation of two distinct solid solutions (Al-poor and Al-rich) is a result of incomplete homogenization during the rapid melting and solidification of the elemental powder blend, despite in situ alloying occurring.
item.limitations: The process parameters were not optimized, leading to notable residual porosity. Heat treatment caused undesirable alloy composition changes (depletion of Al and Cr) due to evaporation in the vacuum ampules.
item.future_work: The authors conclude that process parameter optimization rather than post-process heat treatment should be performed to reduce the porosity of samples.
quotes: The main conclusion is that the production of the Al0.5CrMoNbTa0.5 multi-principle alloy from elemental powder blends using SEBM technique is achievable, but the process parameter optimization rather than post-process heat treatment should be performed to reduce the porosity of samples.
It can be seen from Table 3 that a notable amount of Al evaporated through the printing process: the as-built sample contains only 8.4 at % Al instead of the designed 12.0 at %.
The observed decrease in Al and Cr content through heat treatment is caused by the alloy depletion of these elements in the environment of a vacuum in the ampules.
